column7: deleteProjectCascade's #2656 project FOR UPDATE was written with GORM's default scope, which appends deleted_at IS NULL, so on an ALREADY-deleted project it matched zero rows and locked NOTHING -- exactly the case where a concurrent RestoreProject has to be excluded. RestoreProject took no project-row lock either; the row was locked only by its own final UPDATE, after both child UPDATEs had run. Every other cascade statement is deleted_at IS NULL-scoped too, so under READ COMMITTED the sweeps skipped (snapshots saw deleted children), the restore committed, and the cascade's final UPDATE projects took a fresh statement snapshot, saw the project live and deleted it -- leaving every restored environment and secret LIVE under a deleted project, which no serial order produces. Consequences are #2702/#2710/#2712's: reachable via global-scope roles, ACLs and the owner short-circuit, never purged, outlives the project purge. Fixed by locking the project row by id UNSCOPED on both sides, before any child write, with the cascade reading its liveness verdict off the row it just locked instead of folding deleted_at IS NULL into the locking query -- that folding is what made the lock vacuous. The guard checks Unscoped() specifically, because a guard asserting only "takes clause.Locking" would have been GREEN for the bug's entire lifetime; it also pins the premise that locking in the shared cascade covers both DeleteProject and DeleteProjectIfEmpty (#528). Red-proven by reverting Unscoped() while keeping the lock -- the original defect verbatim -- which the guard reports by name. #2724's second path (RestoreProject does not take EnvironmentSecretGuardLockKey) is recorded in the INVARIANTS fragment and left open: its precondition is a live environment under a deleted project, which is the #2702/#2710 state that #2881 closes
